paper.title: MD-HIT: Machine learning for material property prediction with dataset redundancy control
paper.research_summary: This paper addresses the problem of overestimated machine learning model performance in material property prediction caused by dataset redundancy—i.e., highly similar materials in databases like Materials Project due to historical 'tinkering' in material design. It proposes MD-HIT, a redundancy reduction algorithm inspired by bioinformatics' CD-HIT, with two variants: MD-HIT-composition (using composition-based distance metrics like Mendeleev and MatScholar) and MD-HIT-structure (using structure-based metrics like XRD and OFM features). The authors apply MD-HIT to generate non-redundant datasets for formation energy and band gap prediction, demonstrate that models trained on such datasets show lower (but more realistic) performance on random test sets, and crucially, improved out-of-distribution (OOD) prediction capability—validating that redundancy control enables fairer evaluation and better extrapolation.

evidence.text: In this paper, we survey the overestimated ML performance in materials science for material property prediction and propose MD-HIT, a redundancy reduction algorithm for material datasets.
We propose and develop two material dataset redundancy-reducing algorithms based on a greedy algorithm inspired by the peer bioinformatics CD-HIT algorithm.

stages.stage_goal: Generate non-redundant composition datasets by iteratively selecting representative materials based on composition similarity thresholds

evidence.text: Our MD-HIT-composition and MD-HIT-structure redundancy reduction algorithms are designed based on this idea, utilizing greedy incremental algorithms. In our case, MD-HIT starts the selection process with a seed material (default to H2O) and then sorts the remaining materials by the number of atoms instead of the formula lengths. Subsequently, it classifies each material as redundant or representative, depending on its similarity to the existing representatives already selected into the cluster.
MD-HIT-composition algorithm for redundancy reduction of composition datasets

stages.stage_goal: Generate non-redundant structure datasets by iteratively selecting representative crystal structures based on structure similarity thresholds

evidence.text: MD-HIT-structure algorithm uses the same greedy adding approach as the MD-HIT-composition, except that it uses a structure-based distance metric.
MD-HIT-Structure algorithm for redundancy reduction of structure datasets

stages.stage_name_raw: OOD performance validation using EmbeddingOOD test set
stages.stage_goal: Assess whether redundancy control improves out-of-distribution generalization by constructing an OOD test set based on latent representations
stage_output: comparative MAE/R2 for ID vs. OOD

evidence.text: To compare the true OOD performance of models trained on non-redundant and redundant dataset, we prepared another OOD test set named EmbeddingOOD. First, we used a pretrained Roost model as an encoder to obtain the latent representations for all samples in the entire dataset (86,740 samples). We then calculated the pairwise distances of all samples using their latent representations and selected 1000 OOD samples that are furthest away on average from their three nearest neighbors, forming our EmbeddingOOD test set.

stages.stage_goal: Demonstrate that models trained on non-redundant data achieve superior OOD performance despite lower ID performance
stage_output: MAE/R2 improvements on OOD set (10.03% MAE, 31.6% R2)

evidence.text: Figure 8 shows the performance of two Roost models on two test sets (ID and OOD sets). The MAE of the Roostred increases from 0.1278 eV on the random-split test set to 0.4089 eV for the EmbeddingOOD test set... In contrast, for Roostnr, its MAE increased from 0.1994 eV to 0.3679 eV... However, we find that the Roostnr significantly outperforms Roostred model, with 10.03% improvement in MAE and a 31.6% improvement in R2 for the OOD test set.

dataset_uses.purpose: Source dataset for composition-based redundancy reduction using MD-HIT-composition algorithm

evidence.text: We downloaded 125,619 cif files with material structures from the Materials Project database, which includes 89,354 materials with unique compositions. In cases where compositions corresponded to multiple polymorphs, we adopted average material property values by default, with the exception of formation energy property, for which we used the minimum value. Additionally, we excluded mp-101974 (HeSiO2) due to issues with calculating Matscholar features. After eliminating formulas with over 50 atoms, we obtained a non-duplicate composition dataset with 86,741 samples and then used different similarity (distance) thresholds to generate non-redundant datasets.
